notes:
Verified 21-Aug-2026, then RE-verified live on 21-Aug-2026 (Phase 2 build) via a fresh browser-driven fetch of the raw response. The re-check corrected an assumption from the first pass: the homepage's scrolling ticker ('.rating-content.simply-scroll-list li', formerly documented as the primary selector) is actually populated by client-side JavaScript — it is NOT present in the raw HTTP response, only in the live DOM after the page's own scripts run. The site does not serve a working HTTPS version (https:// redirects back to http://) — use the http URL. SECOND CORRECTION (21-Aug-2026, after the first live GitHub Actions run returned EXTRACTION_ERROR): the site's card wrapper changed from a CSS class '.smallBox3' to an HTML id (id="smallBox3") on a element now carrying the class 'ratebox-table-wrap' instead. This is exactly the 'SOURCE STRUCTURE MAY HAVE CHANGED' scenario the project brief anticipated (section 23) — the system correctly reported EXTRACTION_ERROR rather than showing stale or fabricated data as LIVE.

PHASE 42 (27-Aug-2026) — liveRateUrl and extraction strategy both changed. The project owner reported the dashboard permanently showing VND as SIMULATED for this source and attached a screenshot of a real VND row ("Viet Nam / 1M Vietnam Dong ( VND )", Buy 155.30 / Sell 157.80) that does not exist on '/Home/rate_board' (the old liveRateUrl, an 8-card page — CNY/JPY/USD/GBP/EUR/HKD/AUD/SGD only, confirmed exhaustively as recently as Phase 38 the day before). The owner identified the actual page it came from: 'index.php?/Home/full_rate_board' (note: NOT the same as '/Home/full_rate_board' without 'index.php?' in front — that path 404s; the site uses CodeIgniter's query-string routing style, 'index.php?/Controller/method'). A live connected-browser session (27-Aug-2026) confirmed: (1) this page is a full ~40-currency table, a superset of the old 8-card page — every one of the old 8 currencies' Buy/Sell figures match the old page's numbers exactly (e.g. CNY 60.20/60.47 both places), so this migration changes nothing about those 8, it only adds coverage; (2) it genuinely lists all 12 of this app's supported currencies by ISO code, including the 4 that were previously believed entirely unavailable from this source — VND, THB, KRW, TWD; (3) the values are present in the RAW HTTP response (confirmed via fetch(location.href) from within the live page, independent of any JS execution — same 'no browser required' situation as the old page); (4) every currency's per-unit convention on this page (CNY/HKD/THB/TWD quoted per 100, JPY/KRW per 1000, VND per 1,000,000, everything else per 1 — see each row's own label text, e.g. '100 Chinese Renminbi ( CNY )', '1M Vietnam Dong ( VND )') matches backend/validation/bnmCrossCheck.js's existing ADAPTER_CURRENCY_UNIT map exactly, with zero rescaling needed. Because this page prints each currency's own ISO code directly in its row text, the matching strategy changed from currencyDisplayNames lookup (fragile, needed a hand-maintained entry per currency) to direct code extraction (see primarySelector.matchStrategy below) — the same strategy Taj Muhabath and Jalinan Duta already use. currencyDisplayNames below is kept only as a historical record of what Phase 2/37/38 captured from the old page; parseHtml() no longer reads it.
requiresBrowserAutomationReason: The full_rate_board table's BUY/SELL values were confirmed present in the raw server-rendered HTML via a fetch independent of any browser JS execution (verified 27-Aug-2026, Phase 42, the same way the old rate_board page was originally verified). A plain HTTP GET + HTML parser (cheerio) is sufficient for the primary path.
playwrightFallbackReason: If the site migrates this page to client-side rendering in the future, plain-fetch extraction will start failing validation (fails safe, never silently stale). The Playwright fallback re-uses the exact same selectors against the rendered DOM of the same URL, so it keeps working whether or not JS involvement changes.
branchNotes: No branch/location selector was found on the public site; My Money Master publishes a single site-wide rate per currency.

primarySelector.description: Phase 42 (27-Aug-2026): the desktop rate table on 'index.php?/Home/full_rate_board' — a 'div.table-responsive.rate-board-table' wrapping 'table.table', body id 'ajaxval', one 'tr.filtersearch' per currency (there is also a separate compact/mobile table on the same page, tbody id 'ajaxmobval', with only 3 cells and no country name — NOT used here, since it carries the same data with less context). Each row has 5 <td> cells: [0] 'td.currency-tbody-wrap' containing a 'span.currency-txt' whose text is '<Country name> <unit quantity> <Currency name> ( <ISO CODE> )' (e.g. 'Viet Nam 1M Vietnam Dong ( VND )', 'China 100 Chinese Renminbi ( CNY )'); [1] Buy rate (plain text); [2] Sell rate (plain text); [3] 'at HH:MM AM/PM' (this row's own last-updated time — no date; the page's own top banner shows the date once for the whole table); [4] a 'more info' link, unused.
primarySelector.matchStrategy: For each 'tr.filtersearch' row, read the currencyTextSelector span's text and apply codeExtractPattern to pull the ISO-ish code out of the trailing parentheses (uppercased before comparing). This is a CODE match, not a display-name match — same strategy as Taj Muhabath/Jalinan Duta (see frontend/app.js's CODE_MATCHED_SOURCES). Within the matching row, td[buyCellIndex] and td[sellCellIndex] are the numeric Buy/Sell values; td[lastUpdatedCellIndex] is this row's own 'at HH:MM AM/PM' text (parsed as a same-day time only — see backend/scrapers/mymoneymaster.adapter.js's header comment for why sourceTimestamp is left null rather than guessing which day it refers to).
primarySelector.sampleMatchedText: Viet Nam 1M Vietnam Dong ( VND ) | Buy 155.30 | Sell 157.80 | at 09:50 AM
primarySelector.liveSampleObservedAt: 2026-08-27 (Phase 42, real connected-browser session, both get_page_text and a targeted javascript_tool DOM walk against the live rendered page — table/row/cell class names and the VND row's exact cell contents both confirmed this way, not guessed). Representative values captured that session: AUD 2.886/2.905, CNY 60.20/60.47, EUR 4.678/4.700, GBP 5.47/5.495, HKD 51.40/51.60, JPY 25.25/25.54, KRW 2.925/2.955, SGD 3.163/3.175, THB 12.30/12.40, TWD 12.415/12.495, USD 4.0235/4.038, VND 155.30/157.80 — all 12 of this app's supported currencies present and correctly scoped to their configured ADAPTER_CURRENCY_UNIT (backend/validation/bnmCrossCheck.js).

currencyDisplayNames._deprecatedNote: Phase 42 (27-Aug-2026): this map is no longer read by parseHtml() — matching switched to direct ISO-code extraction (see primarySelector.matchStrategy) once the adapter moved to the full_rate_board page, which prints each row's own code. Kept only as a historical record of the display-name strings captured from the old '/Home/rate_board' page for CNY/JPY/USD/GBP/EUR/HKD/AUD/SGD.

secondarySelector.description: DEMOTED as of the Phase 2 re-verification — this was originally documented as the primary selector, but is confirmed to require JavaScript execution (not present in the raw HTTP response). Kept here only as the target for the Playwright fallback path, or if a future adapter revision prefers it once JS-rendered.
secondarySelector.note: Confirmed via fetch(location.href) from within the live page context returning HTML that does NOT contain this element or text, while document.querySelector('.rating-content li') against the already-loaded DOM does. A raw HTTP GET (no JS) will not see this ticker's content. Superseded as a fallback target by full_rate_board itself (Phase 42) — this ticker doesn't list VND/THB/KRW/TWD either, so it would not help even if used.

waitStrategy.httpFetch: none required for the primary (full_rate_board table) selector — values are present on initial response
waitStrategy.playwrightFallback: navigate to liveRateUrl, wait for 'div.table-responsive.rate-board-table table tbody tr' to be attached, then read as with the HTTP path (same selectors, rendered DOM)

validation.notes: Range is a sanity bound only, not a hard limit — widen per-currency ranges as real historical data accumulates. Reject a reading where BUY > SELL, or where the value looks like it's missing the relevant unit scaling for that currency. JPY range added 26-Aug-2026 (Phase 37). USD/GBP/EUR/HKD/AUD/SGD ranges added 26-Aug-2026 (Phase 38). VND/TWD/THB/KRW ranges added 27-Aug-2026 (Phase 42), deliberately reusing the exact same bounds already in production for these four currencies at Merchantrade Asia (config/websites/merchantradeasia.json) rather than inventing new ones — same currency, same real-world market, no reason for a different sanity window per source.

compliance.robotsTxt: not found (404) as of 21-Aug-2026, re-confirmed 27-Aug-2026 (Phase 42, live browser check of /robots.txt — still 404) — no machine-readable crawl restriction in place for either rate page on this domain.
